description:
RESTATED 2026-09-03 after a scoping pass at dd07432db (fz-kdt.179, .194 and
.199 landed). STEP 1 IS DONE, folded by fz-kdt.179: the seat gate
compiler2_dispatch_seats_the_covering_arm_where_one_covers,
SELECTION_SEAT_ALLOWANCE, BLIND_ESCAPE_POPULATION,
BLIND_ESCAPE_PAIRS_ARRIVAL_KEPT and BLIND_ESCAPE_PAIRS_BY_ARM_ORDER are all
gone, and the law now lives in specificity_order`s two debug_asserts
(only_separated_pairs_moved, every_inversion_covers, callsite_dispatch.rs:263
and :268), which run on every callsite AND every wrapper member selection of
every debug compile.

WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS THE WHOLE PRIZE: the blind-escape census gate drives
its 22 fixtures under SIX arm seeds plus settled, and every seed reads the
SAME pairs with the SAME verdicts. Measured: settled walks 87 pairs (36
Separated, 51 Covering, 0 Escaping); all seven arrivals walk 609 = 87 x 7
exactly, histogram scaling exactly 7x. That is expected BY CONSTRUCTION since
fz-kdt.194 gave separated pairs a canonical order and pinned artifact
arrival-invariance in its own gate: a census OF THE ARTIFACT is
arrival-invariant too, so six seeds were six readings of one fact.

THE CHANGE: drive the census at settled + ONE seed (arms:6 -- the seed that
once aborted enum_map_family and enum_predicate_search) instead of six. Keep
the loop; it is still the permutation ratchet. Rewrite the gate`s
"WHY IT IS DRIVEN UNDER SEEDS" doc with the measured derivation above, and
record an INJECTION RECIPE for its emptiness in the same doc (today the
blind-escape census and INDISTINGUISHABLE_ARM_POPULATION record historical
prose but no injection, unlike fz-kdt.194`s gate which records 66-findings-at-
four-settings).

MEASURED PRIZE (this machine, debug, machine to itself): the census gate is
the lib suite`s critical path -- skipping that ONE test takes the suite from
213.12 s to 125.23 s. Of its 127.98 s, 110 s is the six-seed drive. After the
change: gate 40.15 s, lib wall 126.07 s. That is -87 s of every lib run from a
nine-character edit, with no law deleted.

REJECTED, BOTH MEASURED: settled-only (census 17.46 s, lib 115.41 s) gives up
every permuted reading for 11 s -- not worth it. Deleting the loop and instead
widening ARM_ORDER_ARTIFACT_CENSUS by the 12 fixtures it lacks is GREEN (all
12 are already arrival-invariant) but costs 62.22 s and, because libtest
schedules it late, produced a WORSE lib wall of 169.13 s.

STEP 2 (delete the corpus walk in compiler2_dispatch_lists_its_bodies_in_the_
graphs_first_match_order, keep the property as one unit test over a
constructed PatternDispatchPlan) is still valid and still worth doing -- 22
fixtures, 244 plans, 15.5-15.8 s serial -- but it hides under the arm-order
gate and costs ~0 s of lib WALL clock, so it is CPU honesty, not the prize.
It is a separate commit and does not belong to this one.

STEP 3 IS WITHDRAWN: there is no residue left to name (blind-escape census 87
pairs / 0 escaping; INDISTINGUISHABLE_ARM_POPULATION is `&[]` over 13
fixtures). Do NOT collapse the two gates into one ratchet -- they measure
DIFFERENT relations (is a seat blind, versus do two arms ask one question)
over different fixture lists (22 vs 13) at very different costs (128 s vs
8.6 s). Both stay as emptiness ratchets.
STEP 4 is moot (see fz-kdt.187`s restatement: the extended reader is
recommended against, so SOURCE_ORDER_PLANS_ON_THE_CENSUS stays as the honest
denominator). STEP 5 is not yet: fz-kdt.131 still has no live source
reproducer.

ACCEPTANCE: lib wall 213 s -> ~126 s with the suite green; the gate`s doc
carries the 609 = 87 x 7 derivation and an injection recipe. Concordant:
fz-kdt.195 -- and the prizes are DISJOINT and now quantified. 415 drives
across the 7 corpus gates are 258 distinct (fixture, arrival) pairs, so a
perfect per-pair cache (195) removes 157; but the six census seeds are
DISTINCT arrivals, so no cache can touch them -- only this deletion can. After
this lands, 195 is a CPU-honesty ticket, not a wall-clock one.

comments.text: fz-kdt.183 landed (2e0bb2706): a new cost to own. InputDemand is a fact that MOVES: a function whose forwarding cone is still filling publishes a demand that climbs the lattice, and every activation keyed off it rebases. Three lenses: shift wakes 17 -> 30 / 1 -> 5 / 6 -> 25; rebased completions 19 -> 127 / 2 -> 22 / 10 -> 77; AnalyzeActivation +4/+11/+10; uncaused empty throughout. DeriveInputDemand ran exactly 2x per function at base; now long-tailed (max 17 on one function) because the cone walk restarts from scratch on every re-entry. Bounded by lattice height and cone depth; settling the demand before the first key is minted is the cure. ALSO ungated: World's evidence-collapse read of forwarded_dispatch -- flipping it to local_dispatch moves nothing on 597 fixtures (0 canon movers, 5282 executables). Either the read is inert (fold-concordant: delete it) or the corpus lacks the shape; decide with a witness, not a comment.

fz-kdt.179 landed (c3e27143d) and FOLDED YOUR STEP 1: member selection now runs through routable_alternatives, so the static seat census is retired. Deleted here: the seat gate (compiler2_dispatch_seats_the_covering_arm_where_one_covers) + SELECTION_SEAT_ALLOWANCE; BLIND_ESCAPE_POPULATION, BLIND_ESCAPE_PAIRS_ARRIVAL_KEPT, BLIND_ESCAPE_PAIRS_BY_ARM_ORDER. The blind-escape gate is now an assert-empty ratchet (proven non-vacuous: inject an escape → it fails and the tripwire returns to 12). The law lives in specificity_order's debug_assert as you specified. STILL OPEN (your steps 2-4): SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP_CENSUS is kept as an all-zero ratchet (step 4 -- decide whether the dynamic tripwire is redundant now); INDISTINGUISHABLE_ARM_POPULATION stays at 44 (fz-kdt.107's named residue, not retired); the ARM_ORDER_CENSUS corpus walks (your ~120s prize) are untouched. Re-scope this ticket to what remains.

title: Retire the static seat census once member selection runs through the seat: the law lives in specificity_order's debug_assert, the census keeps only the named residue
